title: Consider the lilies
hook: Solomon in all his glory wasn't dressed like one of these (Matthew 6:28–29)

segments.voice: Yesterday, firmament, the sky that speaks with no words. Your line was day unto day uttereth speech. What was the sky saying? This week we closed forgiveness and opened awe by looking up. Today we look down, at something small. Day one thousand one.

Most feet step right over it: a weed growing out of a crack in the sidewalk, with one yellow flower. Nobody planted it. Nobody waters it. Everyone is on the way to somewhere important. In the Sermon on the Mount, Matthew's Gospel has Jesus point his listeners at exactly this kind of thing: not a temple, not a sunset, but wildflowers in a field. And he sets them beside a king: Solomon, in all his glory. The flowers, he says, win.
screen: `A WEED IN A CRACK.` → `WILDFLOWERS IN A FIELD.` → `THE FLOWERS WIN.`

segments.voice: First, the instruction. In the King James words: "Consider the lilies of the field, how they grow; they toil not, neither do they spin". Consider is the verb. Not glance at, not admire in passing. Look long enough to see how they grow. Second, the comparison: "And yet I say unto you, That even Solomon in all his glory was not arrayed like one of these." All that wealth, all that work, and a flower that did nothing outdressed it. Awe here doesn't come from size. It comes from looking closely at something ordinary until it stops being ordinary. Third, the setting. The lilies sit inside a passage about worry. Just before them come the birds: "they sow not, neither do they reap, nor gather into barns; yet your heavenly Father feedeth them." Just after them, the grass of the field, "which to day is, and to morrow is cast into the oven". The flowers don't last. That's part of the point. Something that won't be here next week is still dressed with care today. Fourth, where it lands: "Take therefore no thought for the morrow: for the morrow shall take thought for the things of itself." In the passage, take no thought is about worry, not about planning. For Christians, the lilies point to God's care. For anyone, they offer a small door out of tomorrow's list and into this one living thing, right now.
screen: `CONSIDER: LOOK LONG ENOUGH.` · `MORE THAN SOLOMON'S GLORY.` · `HERE TODAY, GONE TOMORROW.` · `NO THOUGHT FOR THE MORROW.` · then, large: `CONSIDER THE LILIES.`

segments.voice: Find one flower. A houseplant, a weed outside, a bouquet, or, if there's nothing near, a leaf, or a photo of a flower. Hold your attention on it as if you'd been asked to describe it to someone who has never seen one. The color at the center, and how it changes toward the edge. The shape of each petal. Where the stem bends. Whether it's whole or a little torn. Breathe slowly while you look. When your mind slips back to tomorrow's list, notice that, and return to the flower. If you pray, you can let the looking become thanks. The bell holds the time.
Solomon. The king in all his glory, whom Jesus said was not arrayed like a single wildflower that does no work. Today's word.
Your line: dressed better than a king. When worry about tomorrow arrives today, find one small living thing nearby and look at it for three breaths. Day one thousand one.

howItsDone: Christians read this passage from the Sermon on the Mount as a teaching on trust in God's care; some people on other paths use it as a prompt to spend a few minutes studying one plant or flower closely.

fork.setup: Jesus wants to show how well the lilies are dressed. who does he compare them to?
options: the high priest in his robes.
fork.reveal: Solomon in all his glory, and the wildflower still wins.

original.note: Greek: lilies of the field, from Matthew 6:28.

trapdoor: what you thought: consider the lilies means admire some pretty flowers.
what it means: look closely at a wildflower that does no work, dressed better than a king.
what a scholar hears: the next verse calls them the grass of the field, here today, in the oven tomorrow.

notes: Audit: Matthew 6:26-34 KJV quotations checked word for word; no change.

Hook: Solomon's palace and robes 'the stuff of legend' and 'the grandest figure his hearers knew' (also the fork reveal 'richest king his hearers knew of') are framing, not stated in Matthew 6; 1 Kings 10:23 says Solomon exceeded all the kings of the earth for riches. Trim if the auditor prefers.
'In the passage, take no thought is about worry, not about planning' reads the KJV phrase by its context; a Keeper may want to confirm.
Greek κρίνα τοῦ ἀγροῦ (Matthew 6:28) and transliteration should be checked; which flower 'lilies' means is not claimed.
Week-end review (days 995–1001) is brief: forgiveness closed, awe opened.

Editor: cut 'the grandest figure his hearers knew' / 'stuff of legend' and 'the richest king' in the fork reveal (superlatives not in Matthew 6); hook opening reworded so it doesn't open with a bare scene-list like day 999.
